These derangements were codified for Dark Medieval Malkavians, whose dementia rarely resembles the tidy categories mortal physicians assign it. As with all derangements, they should only be taken with Storyteller consultation, and always feel entirely rational from the character's own perspective.

  • @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.rules-reference-st.JournalEntry.7d3c86953d4f4dd6]{Compulsion}: Your madness manifests as an overwhelming need to perform a specific act, an impulse that eventually consumes you — anything from crossing yourself every time you hear Caine's name to clawing at imaginary insects beneath your skin. Unlike the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.derangements.JournalEntry.d2018925d46840e1]{Obsessive/Compulsive} derangement's fixation on controlling one aspect of life, @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.rules-reference-st.JournalEntry.7d3c86953d4f4dd6]{Compulsion} is rooted in a single, specific, repeated act that must be performed once triggered, growing more consuming and disruptive the longer it is denied.
  • @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.rules-reference-st.JournalEntry.b09a83767c1c4336]{Lunacy}: Your madness ebbs and flows with the cycle of the moon, alternating between contemplative catatonia and fevered mania like the tides. During the dark of the moon, a melancholy grips you, leaving you withdrawn and lethargic and assailed by increasingly dire visions and omens as the moon waxes. At the height of the full moon, a fury overcomes you: a mania that will not let you stay still for long, with voices cascading through your head and driving you further into madness until the moon begins to wane once more. A Narrator may adjust frenzy and Rötschreck difficulties by plus or minus one Trait to reflect the character's current point in the cycle.
  • @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.derangements.JournalEntry.0f264c2a569b4323]{Visions}: Images from beyond plague you without warning, leaving you spent and worn out. When they come, you enter a near-catatonic state of ecstatic pleasure, excruciating torment, or both, rambling incoherently while others can only guess at what you are seeing. Once the vision passes and your senses return, you remember only fleeting glimpses and fragments, recalled later only as an unsettling sense of deja vu; what you do recall is often more frightening than the vision itself.
